site.name: Callum Beadle (Żochowski)
site.title: Environment Artist
about: Currently at SludgePipeGames, the indie studio behind Sparedevil, where I look after head and quality control the level environment art.
Before that I worked at Digital Salmon on real-time projects, from a stylised internal game to a UE5 vehicle experience for Ford™, where I first led a modelling team and helped build its pipeline.
My work runs from whole playable levels down to the tileable materials inside them, and I enjoy building kits that let a team move fast without losing a consistent style.

experience.name: Digital Salmon
experience.detail: Environment Artist. Art direction on Darkest Fayte, modelling team lead on Ford Explorer™

projects.title: Anura: The Smuggler's Path
projects.tagline: A fully playable Unreal Engine 4 level for an RPG about frogs
projects.video_title: Anura // RPG Frog Game // Full Trailer
summary: "The Smuggler's Path" is my fully playable level from our second-year university project, Anura, created in UE4. It runs through four spaces, each with its own job to do.

sections.title: Bandit Camp
sections.text: I had a lot of fun designing this part, especially the pillar centrepiece.

sections.title: Drain Chamber
sections.text: A fun challenge: creating an environmental puzzle to progress, while also making room for a small arena-like area where combat would take place.

sections.title: Flooded Hall
sections.text: I wanted to take advantage of the beautiful water material we had and try something different.

sections.title: Boss Room
sections.text: The final section of the level. It had to feel grand, but also storied and lived in, and I wanted it to radiate a sense of danger and hostility.

projects.title: Ford Explorer™ CX740S
projects.tagline: A real-time, pixel-streamed vehicle experience in Unreal Engine 5
projects.role: Vehicle modelling and texturing, modelling team lead
summary: By far one of my best experiences at Digital Salmon, built in collaboration with Imagination. I was responsible for modelling and texturing this vehicle for a real-time, pixel-streamed experience in UE5 for Ford™.

I also helped lead the modelling team throughout. It was my first time leading others, and helping to build and then manage a pipeline. It was a tough challenge, and I could not be more proud of what we achieved.

projects.title: OMEN
projects.tagline: Sculpted props rendered with Nanite in Unreal Engine 5
summary: A collection of renders using props I sculpted and designed for my final-year project, taking advantage of UE5's Nanite to maximise the quality of the sculpts.
I used the project to learn a more cinematic approach to a game engine and to game art in general. One of the models was made in Substance Designer, before Designer's 3D modelling tools existed.

projects.title: Turbo Tank
projects.role: Environments, level design and kit building
summary: An internal game project at Digital Salmon, and a great opportunity for the team to try developing our own game. Stylised art wasn't normally in our wheelhouse, so it was a fun challenge to explore.

I was responsible for the environments, level design and a kit of structural pieces and props to build out new levels and challenges fast. Houdini proved to be a great tool for this. The project also taught me a lot about optimisation, as we aimed for a stable, high framerate.

projects.title: Sparedevil
projects.tagline: Hellish bowling, built on ancient Greek architecture
summary: Sparedevil is our debut FPS, made together at our newly founded indie studio, SludgePipeGames. Three months from initial concept to release, it was a wild ride that taught me so much as an individual and as a team member.

We chose an economic style, both as a fun creative constraint and to keep a realistic scope for releasing our first game independently on a near non-existent budget. Bowling being the game's theme let us use retro bowling animations as our main inspiration, giving it a quirky style that stayed simple and easy to optimise.

I was primarily responsible for level design and environment art design, and found a lot of enjoyment in a spin on ancient Greek architecture adapted with hellish bowling motifs and finishes. I also modelled and designed a range of the enemy pins, plus some of the unlockable tileable patterns for the customisation system.

sections.title: Risky Rings
sections.text: The game's fourth and most recent map.

sections.title: Asset Kit
sections.text: The asset kit built throughout the game's development. It let us build new arenas faster while keeping a consistent architectural style.

projects.title: Runaway: Gas Station
projects.tagline: A comic book environment for a student film
summary: Freelance environment work for a final-year student film at the University of Hertfordshire. I was responsible for everything seen here. We aimed for a comic book style, using Spider-Verse and the Love, Death & Robots short "The Witness" as reference.

projects.title: UE Style Study
projects.tagline: An artwork by Azamat Khairov, recreated in Unreal Engine 5
summary: I recently stumbled on the beautiful works of Azamat Khairov and knew I had to try recreating one of the pieces in UE5. It was a fun challenge and good Designer and Painter practice, which is always welcome.

images.caption: Original artwork: expectation 3 by Azamat Khairov

projects.title: The Trail Ends
projects.tagline: A composition, lighting and colour piece
projects.role: Project lead, from initial concept to final piece
summary: An internal project at Digital Salmon, where we were tasked with creating a real-time game art piece. I led it from the initial concept through to working with the team on the end result.
Almost all assets came from Quixel's Megascans, as the focus was not asset creation but demonstrating art capability in composition, lighting and colour. It really pushed me, and I learnt a lot.

projects.title: Darkest Fayte: Sanctum
projects.tagline: A modular dungeon kit for an in-house game
projects.role: Art direction, environment work and level design
summary: An in-house game project at Digital Salmon, and a real learning experience. I was responsible for art directing the game, and for all environment work and level design.
All assets were created in Houdini and textured using Substance Designer. I created a modular environment kit to build expansive dungeons and maps to explore.

credits.role: Help generating the floor in Houdini
credits.name: Benjamin Salmon

projects.title: Modular Church
projects.tagline: A Houdini tool for generating modular building pieces
summary: Made while learning more about Houdini: a tool to generate modular building pieces. Everything is textured with tileables and rendered in Unreal, with foliage from Megascans.

projects.title: Materials
projects.tagline: Made in Substance 3D Designer and rendered in Maverick

sections.title: Anura
sections.text: Tileable materials made for the game. I really found a love for Substance Designer on this project, and especially enjoyed tackling a more interesting pattern with the sewer tiles.

sections.title: Freelance
sections.text: Freelance material work for other student projects at my university, including the award-winning Spire and Uplink, alongside personal pieces I'm most proud of. I learnt a lot alongside some very talented artists, and couldn't miss the opportunity to add the legendary companion cube.

images.caption: Uplink satellite environment by Jamie Callow

sections.title: Molded Flesh
sections.text: Created as freelance work on another student project at my university. They wanted a material they could paint onto characters in Substance Painter and also use around their environments in UE4. Made 100% in Substance Designer and rendered in Maverick. Looking at reference for this was... fun.

sections.title: Nodevember 2020
sections.text: I took part in Nodevember again and although university work meant I couldn't keep up all month, I got a lot further than my first time around and learnt so much more. These are some of my favourite pieces.
